01 / THE SIGNAL

Every movement
starts somewhere.

A neuron collects incoming signals. If its voltage reaches a threshold, it sends a brief electrical pulse: a spike.

TRY IT / 01Teaching model

Can you make this neuron fire?

Start with a weak pulse. Then turn it up, or send several close together.

What do you predict: a spike, or silence?

More controls & explanation +

Close inputs can add together before voltage leaks away. Inhibition subtracts from the input. This small leaky integrate-and-fire model shows that idea; its drawn shape is illustrative.

0.1 ms model step · −52 mV rest · −45 mV threshold. Playback is slowed for observation.

02 / THE CONNECTION

A signal.
A detour.
A different result.

Neurons do more than pass a message along. Some encourage the next neuron to fire. Others act as a brake.

What happens without the brake?

Input neuron · receives the repeated stimulus. Select a neuron to inspect its role.

Run once with the brake connected. Then disconnect it and compare.

This four-cell circuit is built to explain excitation and inhibition. It is not a recovered fly circuit. The dots travelling along connections illustrate signal direction.

Give the signal a body ↓

03 / THE MOVEMENT

A leg moves.
But why?

A leg can move because neurons drive its muscles. It can also move because a spring pulls it back. Now you can test the difference.

TRY IT / 03BANC-derived probe

Bend the leg. Change the cause.

Set a starting pose, add a nudge, then run. Compare the same nudge with the neural output disconnected.

Watch individual neurons +

This build exposes aggregate spikes and selected spike times, not membrane voltage. Named sugar-sensory and feeding-output identities are not mapped here, so activity alone is not evidence of feeding.

What can we actually conclude? ↓

05 / THE BIGGER PICTURE

The point isn't
just to watch.
It's to question.

You changed an input, followed a signal, and disconnected a cause. That is the beginning of computational neuroscience.

01

Connections are evidence.

BANC and FlyWire supply measured wiring. They are distinct datasets and models.

02

A model adds assumptions.

Cell equations, sensory tuning, and joint mechanics determine what the simulation can tell us.

03

Movement needs an explanation.

A rendered fly can animate without neural output. A passive spring can return a leg. Compare conditions before claiming a cause.

Model notes & sources +

The specimen is a procedural male fly; the CNS datasets are from female flies. The body is kinematic, not a validated biomechanical reconstruction. The four-cell circuit and spatial brain layout are illustrations.
